This **list of tallest buildings in Bangkok** ranks buildings in Bangkok, Thailand, by height. As of November 2026 Bangkok has 211 completed [skyscrapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyscraper "Skyscraper") over 150 meters (492 feet) in height, of which 129 are listed on the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat database.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Bangkok#cite_note-1)
Bangkok experienced a building boom in the late 1980s and early 1990s when Thailand experienced rapid economic growth. However, the [1997 Asian Financial Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Asian_financial_crisis "1997 Asian financial crisis") left a visible scar on the city's skyline with many unfinished or abandoned buildings. The [Thai economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Thailand "Economy of Thailand") rebounded in the early 2000s and many projects resumed construction. A new wave of building boom starting from the 2010s and continuing up to the present day was spurred by the development of the city's [mass rapid transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_transit "Rapid transit") systems, with new development concentrated around [MRT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRT_\(Bangkok\) "MRT \(Bangkok\)") and [BTS skytrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BTS_Skytrain "BTS Skytrain") stations.
Magnolias Waterfront Residences at [Iconsiam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iconsiam "Iconsiam"), completed in 2018, is Bangkok's tallest building at 318 metres (1,043 feet), followed by [King Power Mahanakhon Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Power_Mahanakhon "King Power Mahanakhon") at 314 metres (1,034 feet). Several skyscraper projects are currently under construction or in the planning phase, including the 92-storey 437 metres/1,435 feet tall Signature Tower at [One Bangkok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Bangkok "One Bangkok") complex, [Dusit Thani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dusit_Thani_Bangkok "Dusit Thani Bangkok") Residences and Asiatique the Riverfront's Iconic Tower. The latter is designed by [Adrian Smith and Gordon Gill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrian_Smith_+_Gordon_Gill_Architecture "Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Bangkok#cite_note-2) architects of the [Burj Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa") in Dubai.

## Tallest completed buildings
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Bangkok&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Tallest completed buildings")]
This list ranks completed and topped out skyscrapers in Bangkok that stand at least 150m/492 ft based on standard height measurement. This includes spires and architectural details, but does not include antenna masts. An equal sign (=) following a rank indicates the same height between two or more buildings. The list contain buildings within the 50 districts of the [Bangkok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangkok "Bangkok") Metropolis, excluding the surrounding provinces of [Nonthaburi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonthaburi "Nonthaburi"), [Pathumthani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathum_Thani_province "Pathum Thani province"), [Samutprakarn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samut_Prakan_province "Samut Prakan province"), [Nakhon Pathom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakhon_Pathom_province "Nakhon Pathom province") and [Samut Sakhon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samut_Sakhon_province "Samut Sakhon province"), which form part of the [Greater Bangkok Metropolitan Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangkok_Metropolitan_Region "Bangkok Metropolitan Region").
